name: BlendEdge
help_text_if_any: Hermite blend surface trimmed and stitched into the polysurface when both adjacent faces are planar; otherwise added between the two faces as a separate, untouched surface (not stitched in). Continuity=Tangency is a degree-3x3 G1 blend. Continuity=Curvature is a degree-5x3 blend whose cross-boundary second derivative is set to each face's own exact analytic directional second derivative (Ev2Der, not a finite difference), so its curvature vector matches each face's curvature exactly in that direction (numerically verified in tests/test_g2_blend.cpp for both flat and curved faces) - real G2 in the cross-boundary direction, not full surface-wide G2 in every direction, and it silently falls back to the plain G1 tangent at any sample where a face's own parametrization is singular there.

name: BlendSrf

description: Create a blend surface between two surfaces with continuity control.

name: Loft
help_text_if_any: Calls the kernel's exact interpolating Brep::Loft: every selected curve lies exactly on the result (measured and printed), Normal is cubic in the loft direction and Style=Straight is linear (sharp at every section). Curves are first made consistent - open curves reversed to run the same way, closed curves reversed to circulate the same way and re-seamed to the point nearest the previous curve's start; a mix of open and closed curves is refused with the reason. Closed planar curves are capped into a polysurface solid (Cap=Yes, the default; Cap=No leaves the periodic surface). Closed=Yes lofts on from the last curve back to the first (kernel Brep::Loft closed=true: a periodic interpolation through every curve, a closed surface with no ends and no caps; at least three curves, refused with the reason otherwise; recorded in History and editable with EditHistory closed=yes|no; with the default SeamAlign=Yes each closed curve is re-seamed to the start point that best matches the previous curve point for point (minimum twist), and a twist left between the last curve and the first is reported). Loose/Tight aren't distinguishable here and aren't offered. SeamAlign=No uses the sections exactly as given (a closed curve whose start point or direction differs from its neighbour's then twists the wall); the default Yes reverses/re-seams them first. StartTangent=<name> / EndTangent=<name> (curve objects named with SetObjectName; their control points are the wall's dS/dv vectors at the first / last curve, e.g. a copy of a circle section scaled by a and lifted by b is the field (a x, a y, b)) with StartWeight= / EndWeight= (default 1) call the kernel's Hermite-type Brep::LoftWithSectionTangents, exact for rational sections (the tangent curve needs the section's weights, or to be a constant field); two curves with both tangents give a cubic Hermite wall; the sections are used as given, the result is not recorded in History. Spacing=Chord|Uniform|Centripetal chooses the loft-direction station parameters (kernel Brep::LoftSpacing: averaged control-point chord lengths by default, equal parameter steps for Uniform, square-root chord lengths for Centripetal); every spacing interpolates every section exactly, only the shape between sections changes. If the kernel refuses a loft, the older control-point fit is used and the reason printed. Continuity=Position|Tangency|Curvature (G0/G1/G2, with AngleTol= in degrees and CurvTol= in 1/length; none given = everything above unchanged) asks for a click near an edge of an existing surface and calls the kernel's NurbsSurface::LoftMatched: the first or last section (whichever lies nearer that surface) is made identical to the edge and the next rows are rewritten by MatchEdge; the finished uncapped surface is MEASURED along the edge (position gap, tangent angle, cross-edge and Gaussian curvature difference) and every section's deviation from it is printed, and the request is refused with the kernel's reason (G0 not met, a closed section, a loft folding back over the adjacent surface, a degree too low, a measured angle / curvature above tolerance) building nothing. A continuity result is not recorded in History (the reason is printed).

help_text_if_any: Moves the picked surface's boundary control row onto the target (Position); Tangency also aligns the next row's step to the target's tangent/normal. Against a target surface edge, Position/Tangency/Curvature all try the exact kernel::NurbsSurface::MatchEdge() construction first (real NURBS algebra, not moved-and-hoped-for control points) - Curvature additionally matches the cross-boundary second derivative, real G2, not just G1 (see kernel::NurbsSurface::MatchEdge()'s own doc comment). Against a target CURVE (rational arcs and circles included) the exact kernel::NurbsSurface::MatchEdgeToCurve() construction is tried first: the edge becomes the curve exactly and, for Tangency/Curvature, the surface keeps its own cross-boundary tangent (and curvature) along it. Follow=Yes (with Continuity=Tangency or Curvature and a target curve lying on a host surface; you then click the host surface as a third pick) makes the edited surface leave the curve in the HOST's tangent plane - its own cross direction rotated into that plane at its own speed - and, with Curvature, take the HOST's second fundamental form along the curve (G2 to the host) (kernel::NurbsSurface::MatchEdgeToCurveFollowing); rational surfaces work, and a curve that is not on the host is refused with nothing changed. Curvature has no approximate fallback when the exact match itself fails (a periodic or unclamped edge/curve, or a target surface whose degree is too low to carry a curvature row) - it fails closed with a diagnostic rather than silently downgrading to G1/G0.

name: NetworkSrf
help_text_if_any: Two curves give an exact ruled surface. Three or four curves that close into a loop within the document tolerance call the kernel's exact Coons patch (CoonsPatchTriangular / CoonsPatch: all boundaries reproduced exactly, corners within tolerance closed first, any order or direction, measured boundary deviation printed); a set that does not close, or that the kernel refuses, prints why and falls back to the old bilinear Coons patch fitted as a degree-3 surface. Five or more curves that close into a loop within the document tolerance are chained (any order or direction), joined into one loop and trimmed out of the kernel's least-squares NurbsSurface::FitPatch surface as one B-rep face (approximate, not an interpolating Coons patch: the worst deviation from the curves and the trimmed edge's deviation are printed and a miss of the tolerance is flagged); a set that does not close, or whose loop folds over its best-fit plane, prints why and uses the first 4 curves as before. Four or more curves that CROSS in their interiors form a curve network: the kernel (NurbsSurface::FitCurveNetwork) sorts them into two directions by where they meet, requires every curve to meet every curve of the other direction within the document tolerance, fits one NURBS surface (cubic where the net allows) through the curves and the meetings, and prints the measured distance of EVERY input curve from it (approximate least-squares fit over the curves' bounding rectangle, untrimmed); a network that misses the tolerance, whose curves do not all meet, or whose order is not a regular grid prints why and the older behaviour runs. Continuity=Position|Tangency|Curvature (G0/G1/G2, with AngleTol= in degrees and CurvTol= in 1/length; none given = everything above unchanged) asks for a click near an edge of an existing surface and, for a curve network of four or more curves, calls the kernel's continuity-aware FitCurveNetwork: the input curve lying on that edge is fitted with the adjacent surface's tangent plane (and second fundamental form) as a heavily weighted constraint, the finished surface is MEASURED along the edge (position gap, tangent angle, cross-edge and Gaussian curvature difference) and printed, and the request is refused with the kernel's reason when G0 is not met, the adjacent plane is too steep, or the measured angle / curvature / curve deviation exceeds the tolerance. A 2-curve or loop selection has no continuity option (refused with that reason). A continuity result is not recorded in History (the reason is printed).
description: Fit a surface through a network of crossing curves.

name: Shell
help_text_if_any: Hollows a closed solid. With no face clicked to remove/open and no per-face thickness override, a polysurface whose faces are all planar and convex (a box or other simple polyhedron) now calls the kernel's exact ShellConvexPlanar first, giving a real B-rep result (exact volume, no tessellation) instead of a mesh; it fails open to the existing mesh construction (outer minus inward vertex-normal offset) for a curved or non-convex solid, or a thickness beyond that shape's own offset feasibility. Optionally click face(s) of a polysurface solid to remove/open before entering thickness (Enter with none picked keeps the old fully-closed behavior): the picked face(s) are dropped from the outer surface, the remainder gets the inward offset, and a rim mesh connects the two boundary loops - a real open shell (cup/case) for a single face, or a group of mutually-adjacent faces, on a simple box-like solid; a selection that would leave a non-manifold or multi-piece remainder is rejected with a warning rather than producing bad geometry, and mesh-only solids (no polysurface to pick faces on) still only support the fully-closed form. After face removal you can also click additional face(s) and type a thickness for each (repeat, then Enter for the default Thickness on the rest): every kept face's vertices then solve to the exact intersection of its own neighbours' offset planes, so two faces with different thickness meet in a real mitered corner rather than an average - numerically verified for a box (see tests/surface_script.txt) and, by the same plane-intersection algebra, correct for any solid whose kept faces are all planar (prisms and other polyhedra). If any kept face is curved, per-face overrides are detected and dropped for that solid (warned), falling back to the single default Thickness everywhere on it rather than applying an unverified per-triangle offset to a curved surface.

name: Sweep1
help_text_if_any: A single cross section calls the kernel's exact Brep::Sweep1 (rotation-minimizing-frame transport and skin; still an uncapped surface, periodic when the rail is closed, same as before) and records History (History On) for UpdateHistory to rebuild against the rail/section's current shape; two or more cross sections call the kernel's exact Brep::Sweep1Sections (each section anchored on the rail - a closed planar one where the rail crosses its plane - decoded in its rotation-minimizing frame, blended between neighbours and skinned through the stations: every section reproduced exactly, the wall measured against the exact blended sections between stations and held to the document tolerance, retried at up to 256 stations; an uncapped surface; closed cross sections must already share a seam and direction, the kernel refuses seams more than 60 degrees apart; with History On it records {rail, section 1, section 2, ...} and rebuilds when the rail or a section is edited, a rebuild the kernel refuses keeping the old wall with the reason printed); it falls back, with the reason printed, to the old sampled approximation (24 samples per section, fitted to a degree-3 surface) when the kernel refuses (closed rail, a section plane the rail never crosses or contains, two sections at one station, mismatched seams) or misses the document tolerance. Cap=Yes (default No) turns the sweep of a closed planar cross section into a closed B-rep solid with the kernel's own capping (two planar end caps; the section may sit anywhere along the rail and several cross sections are capped too; recorded for History); an open or non-planar section, or a fallback construction, keeps the uncapped surface and prints why. A closed rail that is an exact planar circle is built as the section revolved once about the rail's axis (Brep::Revolve: an exact rational surface, e.g. a true torus, measured against the revolved section and printed), and with Cap=Yes as a closed one-face solid; any other closed rail keeps the kernel's periodic skin.
description: Fit a surface through profile curves and one edge curve.

name: Sweep2

Two or more cross sections call the kernel's Brep::Sweep2Sections (each section decoded in its own station's two-rail frame, blended between neighbours and skinned through the stations: every section reproduced, wall edges within the document tolerance of the rails when the sections touch them, measured and printed; closed cross sections must already share a seam and direction, the kernel does not align them; with History On it records {rail 1, rail 2, section 1, section 2, ...} and rebuilds when a rail or a section is edited, a rebuild the kernel refuses keeping the old wall with the reason printed); it falls back, with the reason printed, to the old approximated two-rail-scaled sweep fitted to a degree-3 surface when the kernel refuses (crossing section anchors, rails that touch at an interior station, a section where the rails touch) or misses the document tolerance; two closed rails give a cyclic sweep whose wall is closed round the ring (seam at the first section, sections ordered round both rails), and rails meeting at an end give a wall pinched to a point there. Cap=Yes (default No) caps a closed planar cross section's sweep into a closed B-rep solid (single section, or the multi-section wall) with the kernel's own capping; anything that cannot be capped keeps the surface and prints why.

name: ToNURBS
help_text_if_any: SubD input: converts to a real multi-patch NURBS Brep via Catmull-Clark limit-surface evaluation (kernel::SubD::ToNurbsPatchesAdaptive) - every face whose 4 corners are ordinary interior (valence-4) vertices becomes the mathematically exact bicubic Bezier patch (the well-known, non-proprietary fact that a regular Catmull-Clark control net *is* a uniform bicubic B-spline lattice; adjacent exact patches share bit-identical boundary curves and join into one seamless polysurface). Faces touching an extraordinary vertex, a crease, or a boundary have no such closed form: after a few rounds of whole-mesh Catmull-Clark pre-refinement (applied automatically, up to 2 rounds bounded by face count), each one is further adaptively split (2 more levels) into progressively smaller exact regular patches around a single still-approximated flat corner patch, rather than left as one coarse flat approximation across the whole original face - those final corner patches stay unjoined at their approximate edges rather than being silently forced to look exact, and the adaptive split itself can introduce further naked T-junction edges where a split patch neighbors an unsplit regular one. The status line reports how many patches of each kind were produced. Mesh input converts exactly (unchanged). Options: FitInterior=Yes (default No) fits the irregular patches' edge curves and interior control points to the limit surface by least squares (corners and shared boundaries unchanged, so the polysurface stays watertight) and prints the measured deviation of both interiors and the fitted patch count; Levels=N (0 = automatic) fixes the number of Catmull-Clark rounds applied first.

Like every Dim* command the geometry is a static bake, not a live object, so nothing here moves on its own. This window closes a related gap for a dimension that is otherwise associative (DimLinear/DimAligned/DimAngle/DimRadius/DimDiameter via UpdateDimensions, cmd_annotate.cpp; DimOrdinate/DimCreaseAngle/DimArea/DimCurveLength/DimVolume via UpdateMeasureDims, cmd_annotate2.cpp): the tolerance suffix used to be silently dropped whenever one of those commands rebuilt the dimension's text from a moved/edited anchor, since the rebuild always started from the fresh measurement alone. name: Patch
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Data within the document tolerance of their own best-fit plane keep the planar patch (an exact plane trimmed by a single closed planar curve, or a least-squares rectangle). Non-planar data call the kernel's least-squares NurbsSurface::FitPatch (boundary samples of the selected curves and the selected points, a bicubic-or-lower net grown until the worst data deviation is within the document tolerance, measured and printed; a surface that misses tolerance is flagged NOT met) and the closed curve enclosing the most area is trimmed out of it by Brep::TrimmedPatchFace, every other closed curve wholly inside it becoming a hole of the same face (overlapping or crossing curves are reported and leave the surface untrimmed); if the kernel refuses or the fit is no better than the flat plane the reason is printed and the planar construction runs. With History On the non-planar result records every selected curve and point (in selection order) and the fit (and trim) is re-run when one is edited; a rebuild that no longer applies (the data became flat, a source deleted, the fit failing) keeps the old patch with the reason printed. Continuity=Position|Tangency|Curvature (G0/G1/G2, with AngleTol= in degrees and CurvTol= in 1/length; none given = everything above unchanged) asks for a click near an edge of an existing surface and calls the kernel's continuity-aware FitPatch: the selected curve lying on that edge supplies ordered edge samples whose adjacent tangent plane (and second fundamental form) enter the least-squares fit as heavily weighted constraints; the finished UNTRIMMED surface is MEASURED between the samples (position gap, tangent angle, cross-edge and Gaussian curvature difference) and printed, and the request is refused with the kernel's reason (G0 not met, adjacent plane too steep, measured angle / curvature above tolerance, data deviation above the document tolerance). A continuity result is not recorded in History (the reason is printed).

name: TitleBlock
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Builds a simple Name/Date/Scale/Sheet field table, not an instance of a linked block definition - inserting one does not track edits to a shared title-block template, the same live-instancing gap as the Block command (cmd_drafting.cpp) has no fix for. Name defaults to (and, without an explicit Name=, stays associative to) the document's own Settings().title, set via the Document Properties panel; Date defaults to (and, without an explicit Date=, stays associative to) today's date; Scale defaults to (and, without an explicit Scale=, stays associative to) the active sheet's own single detail view's current scale, when that sheet has exactly one - UpdateTitleBlock re-pulls any of the three later, independently, if the title, the date, or that detail's scale has changed, and the per-frame associative-annotation callback (Application.cpp) re-pulls them automatically on every document edit, same as the dimension/leader/GD&T/MultiLeader/PanelSchedule families above. An explicit Name=/Date=/Scale= freezes that one field, same as PanelSchedule's Circuits= freezing that table. Sheet still has no equivalent document-level source and stays a static baked field either way (it is merely which layout happened to be active when the title block was placed, not a property the table could re-derive - a layout has no id, only a name).

name: UpdateBillOfMaterials
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-derives every BillOfMaterials table's rows (count/layer/material/length-area-volume) from the current state of the objects it was built from, replacing the old baked rows in place - the associative counterpart to BillOfMaterials's static bake, following the same explicit-recompute shape as UpdateSectionViews above rather than an automatic callback on every document edit.

name: UpdateDimensions
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-evaluates every associative dimension's anchor(s) - DimLinear/DimAligned/DimRotated, DimAngle, DimRadius/DimDiameter, Leader, Centermark, CenterLine - and rebuilds its curve/arrow/text geometry from their current position, replacing the old baked geometry in place - the associative counterpart to those dimension types' static bake, following the same explicit-recompute shape as UpdateSectionViews (cmd_drafting2.cpp) rather than an automatic callback on every document edit. This window fixes a gap in that rebuild for DimLinear/DimAligned, DimAngle and DimRadius/DimDiameter: a DimTolerance suffix (cmd_drafting2.cpp) on one of these used to be silently dropped, since the rebuilt text was always the freshly recomputed measurement alone. It is now diffed against the DimTolerance.Base tag DimTolerance itself leaves and re-appended to whatever the new measurement is (GroupToleranceSuffix/ReapplyToleranceSuffix, annotate_common.h) - a dimension carrying a tolerance keeps it through a move/edit, not just through the DimTolerance command's own idempotent re-run. Leader was never affected (its text is a static label copied verbatim, not recomputed), and Centermark/CenterLine have no text to lose. A later window wires DimLinear/DimAligned/DimAngle/DimRadius/DimDiameter's rebuild to the dimension's own recorded AnnotationStyle by name (StyleParamsByName, annotate_common.h): the style's precision/unit_suffix/ext_offset/ext_extension/text_placement are re-read live on every Update, not just baked in at creation, so editing a style's dimension properties and re-running UpdateDimensions reformats every dimension built with it.

name: UpdateFields
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-evaluates every Field's live value - Filename/FilePath (the document's own Save path), Date (today), CurrentLayer (the document's current layer name), ObjectCount (non-annotation object count), or Length/Area/Volume (summed from its recorded FieldRefIds via the same MeasureOne math DimArea/DimCurveLength/DimVolume use) - and rebuilds its glyph text in place, replacing the old baked text, the same explicit-recompute shape as UpdateDimensions/UpdateMeasureDims/UpdateTitleBlock rather than an automatic callback on every document edit. A field whose Length/Area/Volume source object(s) are all gone or no longer measurable under their kind is skipped and stays at its last baked text, the same dead-reference rule UpdateMeasureDims/BomRefIds use.

name: UpdateGdtSymbols
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-evaluates every FeatureControlFrame/DatumFeature/SurfaceFinish/WeldSymbol's feature-point anchor and rebuilds it from the current position, replacing the old baked geometry in place - the associative counterpart to those four commands' static bake, following the same explicit-recompute shape as UpdateMultiLeaders/UpdateDimensions/UpdateSectionViews/UpdateBillOfMaterials rather than an automatic callback on every document edit.

name: UpdateHatches
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Associative hatch: a hatch made by the Hatch command (Solid or a library pattern) remembers its boundary curve and rebuilds itself to fill the boundary's CURRENT shape and position when that curve is moved, scaled or reshaped - UpdateHatches does it on demand and Application.cpp's per-frame associative-annotation callback does it automatically after every edit. A hatch that was itself moved (alone or together with its boundary) is left where it is and just re-synchronised to the boundary's new state; a deleted or no longer closed boundary leaves the hatch untouched. Not covered: Bitmap hatches, hatches with islands/holes and hatches imported from DXF/DWG/3dm, which stay static, and HatchScale's older 4-pattern rebuild.

name: UpdateHistory
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-runs every recorded construction (see History for the list) against its source object(s)' *current* geometry (moved, reshaped, or control-point-edited since) and replaces that object's geometry in place - same object id, same layer/color/name/user text, only the shape changes. One registry-based dispatch (history_rebuild.h): sources may be curves, surfaces, polysurfaces or the results of other recorded constructions, which are rebuilt first (curve -> Extrude -> BooleanUnion updates in order). A source that was deleted, changed kind, or that the construction now refuses leaves that object exactly as it was, prints the reason, and skips everything built from it. The explicit-recompute shape of ElecRebuild (cmd_elec.cpp) and UpdateDimensions (cmd_annotate.cpp), not an automatic callback on every document edit. Revolve's axis is recorded as-picked and does not move with the curve, matching Rhino. Sweep1/Sweep2 only record from a single cross-section; Revolve Output=SubD, FilletEdge with Rho/RailType/variable radii or the approximate path, ChamferEdge by angle, Project/Pull of a source that splits into several pieces, Shell with opened or individually-thickened faces, mesh/SubD booleans and every other command record nothing. Objects made before History was turned On have no recorded history and are left untouched.

name: UpdateMeasureDims
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-derives DimArea/DimCurveLength/DimVolume (summed from every recorded source object's current shape, MeasureRefIds), DimCreaseAngle (from its two recorded objects' current direction, DimRefObj1/DimRefObj2) and DimOrdinate (per point, FindPointAnchor on the base point and, separately, each feature point - DimOrdinateCommand/BuildOrdinateDimGroup) and rebuilds each leader/text in place - the same explicit-recompute shape as UpdateDimensions (cmd_annotate.cpp) and UpdateTitleBlock/UpdatePanelSchedule/UpdateBillOfMaterials (cmd_drafting2.cpp), not an automatic callback on every document edit. A dimension built before DimOrdinate's associativity was added (no MeasureRefIds/DimRefObj1/DimP0 tag), or one whose recorded object(s) no longer measure under their kind (deleted, or a shape edit made a DimArea curve non-closed etc.), is skipped and stays (or reverts to) a static baked measurement; the leader's landing point (MeasureAt) is kept fixed across an update, only the value and arrowhead position change. A DimOrdinate point that was never anchored still carries its built DimP0/DimP1 points, so it re-lays-out identically rather than being skipped. This window fixes the same DimTolerance-drop gap UpdateDimensions had: a tolerance suffix (cmd_drafting2.cpp DimTolerance) on any of these five kinds used to vanish on rebuild, since the rebuilt text was always the freshly recomputed measurement alone; it is now recovered from the DimTolerance.Base tag and re-appended to the new measurement (GroupToleranceSuffix/ReapplyToleranceSuffix, annotate_common.h), same fix, same helpers, shared with UpdateDimensions.

name: UpdateMultiLeaders
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-evaluates every MultiLeader's per-arrow anchors and rebuilds the arrows/landing/text from their current positions, replacing the old baked geometry in place - the associative counterpart to MultiLeader's static bake, following the same explicit-recompute shape as UpdateDimensions (cmd_annotate.cpp) and UpdateSectionViews/UpdateBillOfMaterials below rather than an automatic callback on every document edit.

name: UpdatePanelSchedule
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-derives every associative PanelSchedule's rows (circuit/description/load) from the current circuit/load assignment (ElecCircuit, cmd_elec.cpp) of the electrical components it was built from - or, for the Enter/'every circuit-assigned component' mode, every currently-assigned component in the document - replacing the old baked rows in place, the same explicit-recompute shape as UpdateBillOfMaterials above. A PanelSchedule built from hand-typed Circuits= text carries neither PanelAll nor PanelRefIds and is left untouched, same as before this change.

name: UpdateTitleBlock
category: Dino extension (not in the Rhino catalog)
help_text_if_any: Re-derives every associative TitleBlock's Name field from the document's current Settings().title (Document Properties), Date field from today's date, and/or Scale field from its own sheet's single detail view's current scale (see TitleBlockCommand's own registration note above for the single-detail scoping), replacing the old baked value(s) in place - the associative counterpart to TitleBlock's static bake, following the same explicit-recompute shape as UpdatePanelSchedule/UpdateBillOfMaterials above, and also run automatically every frame (quiet=true) by Application.cpp's UpdateAssociativeAnnotations callback so an explicit UpdateTitleBlock is no longer required after an edit. All three fields are independent: a TitleBlock built with an explicit Name=/Date=/Scale= (no TitleBlockAuto/TitleBlockDateAuto/TitleBlockScaleAuto tag, respectively) leaves that one field untouched while the others, if still auto, keep updating - same as before this change for a TitleBlock with none of the three tags.
